title: Lower bounds for Naslund's crossing problem
abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib proofs of the first lower bounds above the trivial bound n for Naslund's crossing problem (J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 174 (2020), Problem 12). P(n) is the least r + s such that the tensor [x1 = x4][x2 = x3] on [n]^4 is a sum of r tensors of rank one along {12|34} and s tensors of rank one along {13|24}; in matrix form, the least rank B + rank R(C) over all splittings S_n = B + C of the swap matrix, where R is the realignment. Over every field the project proves P(n) ≥ 4n/3 for n ≥ 3, P(n) ≥ 15n/11 for n ≥ 5, P(n) ≥ 67n/49 for n ≥ 7, P(n) ≥ n + 3 for n ≥ 4, P(5) ≥ 8, P(6) ≥ 9, and P(4) = 7 (with a split that attains 7). The results are original.
